column3: Close to the Greek; “cellar” is rendered “a secret place.”
NKJV has “Therefore, when your eye is good,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is clear ….”
Close to the Greek; “plundering” is rendered “greed.”
Close to the Greek; “the things within” is rendered “such things as you have.”
NKJV includes “scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “Woe to you!”
NKJV includes “their tombs,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “you build.”
Close to the Greek; “the house” is rendered “the temple.”
NKJV has “as He said these things to them,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “when He went out from there.”
NKJV includes “seeking” and “that they might accuse Him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “lying in wait to catch something from His mouth.”
